outcome: vertical transmission of hepatitis B virus (HBV)
cohort: The study included 201 couples where the father was HBV DNA-positive and the mother was anti-HB-positive before pregnancy, and 188 couples where the father was HBV DNA-positive and the mother was HBsAg-negative and anti-HBs-positive as a control group.
finding: Administering antiretroviral therapy to HBV DNA-positive fathers before pregnancy reduced viral load and prevented father-to-infant HBV vertical transmission, with no significant differences in neonatal outcomes between the two groups.
birth_weight: The study found no statistically significant difference in birth weight between neonates born to couples in the case and control groups.
